newsitem.title: FINLAND: EU's Hansch sees Finnish ERM decision soon - radio.
newsitem.headline: EU's Hansch sees Finnish ERM decision soon - radio.

text.p: European Parliament President Klaus Hansch said on Finnish radio on Thursday he expected Finland to decide "in the next few weeks" whether it would link the markka to Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM).
"My point of departure is that Finland will decide in the next few weeks whether to join ERM," Hansch said in an interview broadcast on Finnish radio on Thursday afternoon.
Hansch is part of a visit by the European Parliament's Socialist group to Finland, hosted by Social Democratic Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen.

An official at the prime minister's office told Reuters Lipponen and Hansch had met privately for a short while on Wednesday afternoon. On Wednesday evening, Lipponen hosted a reception for the visiting Euro MPs.

Lipponen has earlier said the decision whether to join ERM will be made in the near future. Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto has repeatedly said the decision will be made this autumn. He has also said December can be regarded as "the near future".
Niinisto is scheduled to give on Thursday afternoon the government's response to a question by a Finnish MP on the reasoning behind a possible decision to peg the markka to ERM.

Niinisto will address the ERM issue at a question-and-answer session in parliament due to start at 1630 (1330 GMT). According to one political insider who said he had seen the prepared text of Niinisto's response, it was "broadly phrased."
Lipponen is also scheduled to attend the session. On Wednesday, officials close to the prime minister said it was possible he would participate in the debate.
Finland has said it intends to fulfil all criteria for membership of Europe's planned third phase of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), due to start in 1999.

Finland's stated objective is to be in the first wave of countries entering the single currency bloc. Some analysts say a link to the ERM is a condition for meeting the exchange rate stability criterion for EMU.
The Bank of Finland has stressed the importance of not going for a hasty ERM peg.

Pointing at potential turmoil in Europe if austere French and German 1997 budgets, designed to help them meet the EMU public deficit criterion, meet strong opposition, the Bank has said the ERM might not be a stable system.
The Finnish currency has been floating since September 1992.
